target_customer: Commercial concrete contractors doing floor finishing and shotcrete work
problem: Finishing concrete floors is slow, physically hard labor that depends on scarce skilled workers, so contractors wanted robots that let one person do the work of several.
business_model: Hardware robots sold or leased to concrete contractors
product_category: Construction robotics, automated power trowel and shotcrete robot

founders.name: Jim Delaney
founders.background_notes: Joined Built Robotics' engineering team after the 2023 acquisition.

founders.name: Gunner Robinson
founders.background_notes: The YC page gives no further background.

technical_complexity.rationale: An autonomous power trowel needs a custom machine, sensing of concrete cure state and navigation on a live worksite. Hardware plus field reliability is hard for a three person team.

defensibility.rationale: Hardware and know-how plus a patent filing on an autonomous power trowel raised the barrier, but a very small team and early product limited the moat.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Built Robotics acquired the team and technology in January 2023 and planned to discontinue Roin's existing products, with no commitment to a commercial release of the trowel or shotcrete robot.

market_need_then: Construction labor was scarce and concrete finishing is repetitive manual work. No dated demand evidence beyond the company's claim that one person could do the work of six was found.

brand_strength.rationale: No sources show press about the brand, community or merch. Search results confused the name with Robin Technologies, suggesting low recognition.

outcome_analysis: Roin built a concrete power trowel and a shotcrete robot with a three person team and sold to few if any customers publicly. In January 2023 Built Robotics acquired the company, hired the CEO and said Roin's current product line would be discontinued with no commercial release committed, which reads as a technology and team acquisition rather than a commercial success. Deal terms and funding history are not public.
notes: Company site rointech.com returned HTTP 503 during the check so its state is unknown. Funding unverified: CB Insights alone lists about $130K over two rounds with a March 2021 seed, not recorded as a round. Competitor search returned no dated 2021 sources so the list is empty. Acquihire label is an inference from the discontinued product line statement in the press coverage.
